recipes.name: Chicken Pad Thai

ingredients.item: chicken breast or thigh, thinly sliced
garlic chives, cut into 3 cm pieces
lime wedges, ground chilli, extra bean sprouts (to serve)

steps: Soak the rice noodles in plenty of boiling water for about 5 minutes, then drain and rinse briefly under cold water; use them soon after.
Stir the tamarind puree, brown sugar, fish sauce and oyster sauce together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pan on high, add onion and garlic and cook for about 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and fry for roughly 1.5 minutes until mostly cooked through.
Push everything to one side, pour the egg into the empty side, scramble it, then toss through the chicken.
Add bean sprouts, tofu, noodles and the sauce; toss gently for about 1.5 minutes until the noodles have absorbed the sauce.
Toss through garlic chives and half the peanuts, then remove from the heat.
Serve straight away topped with the remaining peanuts, lime wedges, a pinch of chilli and extra bean sprouts on the side.

recipes.name: Thai Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce

ingredients.item: chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut into 2 cm pieces
chopped peanuts, lime wedges, coriander, sliced chilli (to serve)

steps: Mix the chicken with the marinade ingredients (curry powder, sugar, 2 tsp red curry paste, salt) plus 1/4 cup of the coconut milk; rest for at least 20 minutes, or overnight for best flavour.
Thread 4-5 chicken pieces onto each skewer.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high and cook the skewers in batches, about 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
For the sauce, combine the remaining coconut milk with the peanut butter, sugar, red curry paste, dark soy, salt, vinegar and water in a saucepan over medium-low.
Simmer the sauce for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, then thin with water until pourable but thick; keep warm.
Serve the skewers with the sauce on the side for dipping, sprinkled with peanuts, coriander and chilli, with lime and rice alongside.

recipes.name: San Choy Bow (Chinese Lettuce Wraps)
recipes.servings: 3 as a main / ~6 as a starter

ingredients.item: Chinese cooking wine (or mirin / dry sherry)
canned water chestnuts, drained and finely chopped
soft lettuce leaves, crushed peanuts, sliced scallions (to serve)

steps: Blend the cornflour with 1 tbsp of the water until smooth, then mix in the rest of the water, both soy sauces, oyster sauce, sesame oil, wine and sugar.
Heat the peanut oil in a wok or large skillet on high; fry the garlic and ginger briefly, then add the onion and cook for about a minute.
Add the pork mince and cook until it loses its pink colour.
Stir in the carrot, water chestnuts, baby corn and mushrooms; cook for about 2 minutes until the carrot has softened.
Pour in the sauce and cook for around 1.5 minutes until it thickens into a glossy coating over the filling.
Spoon the filling into lettuce leaves, finish with peanuts and scallions, wrap up and eat.

recipes.name: Beef Rendang

ingredients.item: dried chillies, rehydrated (or 12 large fresh red chillies)
lemongrass stalks, white part only, sliced
chuck steak (or other slow-cooking beef), cut into 4 cm cubes
lemongrass stick, bottom half only, smashed
makrut lime leaves, very finely sliced

steps: Blitz all the spice paste ingredients (chillies, onion, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, ginger, 2 tbsp oil) in a food processor until fine.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy-based pot on high and brown the beef in two batches; set the beef aside.
Turn the heat down to medium-low, add the spice paste and fry for 2-3 minutes until darkened and fragrant.
Return the beef to the pot and add the cinnamon, clove, star anise, cardamom, smashed lemongrass, coconut milk, tamarind, lime leaves, desiccated coconut, sugar and salt; stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover with the lid and cook on low for about 1 hour 15 minutes, until the beef is quite tender but not yet falling apart.

Remove the lid and reduce on medium for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally at first and frequently towards the end, until the sauce reduces to a dark paste that coats the beef and the oil separates (this is where the deep colour comes from).
If the beef is not yet fall-apart tender, add a splash of water and keep cooking briefly; serve with coconut rice.
